title: "Python in a post"
description: "Running Python when the post is rendered: figures, tables and numbers in the text that come straight from the data."
author: "Tolborg Group"

A code block written as ```` ```{python} ```` is *run* when the post is
rendered, and whatever it prints or plots ends up in the post. This means that
the figures and numbers in a post are made from the data, rather than copied
in by hand, and that they are updated when the data changes.

The example here is a $k$-point convergence test of a total energy, stored as
`kpoint-convergence.csv` next to this post.

## Reading the data

```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("kpoint-convergence.csv")
df.head()
```

The code runs in the post's folder, so files next to `index.qmd` are read
by their name. The last expression of a block is displayed, as in a Jupyter
notebook, and a data frame is shown as a table.

## Options for a code block

Lines at the top of a block starting with `#|` are *cell options*. They set
how the block and its output are shown, e.g. a label and caption that turn the
output into a numbered table:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-convergence
#| tbl-cap: "Total energy relative to the finest mesh."
#| echo: false
E_ref = df["energy_ev"].iloc[-1]
table = df.assign(error_mev=1000 * (df["energy_ev"] - E_ref))
table.columns = ["k-points per side", "Energy (eV)", "Error (meV)"]
table.style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=3)
```

`echo: false` hides the code and keeps the output, which is what most posts
want for most blocks. Other useful options are `code-fold: true`, which hides
the code behind a "Code" toggle, as in the block below, and `output: false`,
which runs the code without showing anything.

## Figures

A plot made with Matplotlib becomes a figure, and with a `fig-` label it can be
referred to as @fig-convergence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-convergence
#| fig-cap: "Convergence of the total energy with the number of $k$-points per side. The dashed line is the value for the finest mesh."
#| code-fold: true
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(
    df["k_per_side"], df["energy_ev"], "o-",
    color="#0f766e", markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5,
)
ax.axhline(E_ref, color="gray", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--")
ax.set_xlabel("$k$-points per side")
ax.set_ylabel("Total energy (eV)")
ax.set_xticks(df["k_per_side"])
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

## Numbers in the text

A value computed in a block can be written straight into a sentence with
inline code that starts with `python` in braces, as shown below the following
block:

```{python}
#| echo: false
tolerance_mev = 5
converged = table[table["Error (meV)"].abs() < tolerance_mev]
k_converged = int(converged["k-points per side"].iloc[0])
```

The energy is converged to within `{python} tolerance_mev` meV from
`{python} k_converged` $k$-points per side, as seen in @tbl-convergence.

Written in the source, that sentence is

```markdown
The energy is converged to within `{{python}} tolerance_mev` meV
from `{{python}} k_converged` $k$-points per side,
as seen in @tbl-convergence.
```

so changing the tolerance, or the data, changes the text with it.

## When is the code run?

The blog is set up with `freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml`. A post's code is run
when the post is rendered for the first time and again only when its
`index.qmd` changes. The results are stored in the `_freeze/` folder, which is
committed together with the post. This has two advantages:

- Old posts keep working even if the code or data they used has moved on.
- A post can use data that is too large for the repository, or computations
  that only run on the cluster: as long as `_freeze/` is committed, GitHub
  only needs the stored results to publish the blog.

::: {.callout-important}
Remember to commit `_freeze/` together with the post. If the stored results are
missing, the post is run again when the blog is published, which fails if the
data is not in the repository.
:::

## Packages

The code runs in the Pixi environment of the blog. A package that a post needs
is added with

```bash
pixi add scipy
```

and the updated `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock` are committed with the post.
